baysesp

baysesp provides Bayesian estimation of the accuracy (sensitivity, specificity and predictive values) of one or more binary diagnostic tests performed on the same subjects, when the disease status is ascertained by the reference standard only for a subset of them (partial verification).

Estimating accuracy from the verified subjects alone is biased whenever the decision to verify depends on the test results, as it usually does in screening studies. baysesp corrects this verification bias with a joint model for the tests, the disease and the verification process, written in Stan.

Features

  • Joint modeling of K binary tests. The saturated model makes no assumption on how the tests depend on each other; log-linear and random effects models assume a structure for that dependence.
  • Accuracy of combination rules: any test positive, all positive, at least k positive, or a custom rule.
  • Comparisons between tests: differences and ratios of sensitivities and specificities, with their posterior distributions.
  • Verification that depends only on the test results (missing at random) or also on the disease status (missing not at random).
  • Profiles that are never verified, for example when only subjects with a positive test receive the reference standard: the missing information is an explicit prior, with bounds and ratios that hold whatever that prior is.
  • Sensitivity analyses over the assumptions that the data cannot check, without fitting the model again, and prior-posterior comparisons.
  • Two Stan backends: rstan (default, models precompiled at installation) and {cmdstanr} (optional).

Installation

You can install the development version of baysesp from GitHub with:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("giovannitinervia9/baysesp")

Installing the package compiles its Stan models and takes a few minutes.

To use the optional {cmdstanr} backend, install {cmdstanr} and CmdStan and compile the models once with compile_models():

baysesp::compile_models()

Example

Two tests, A and B, are performed on 3000 simulated subjects; those negative to both tests are rarely verified.

library(baysesp)

set.seed(2026)
study <- simulate_study(
  n = 3000,
  prevalence = 0.15,
  sensitivity = c(A = 0.85, B = 0.70),
  specificity = c(A = 0.90, B = 0.95),
  verification_prob = c(0.1, 0.8, 0.8, 1)
)

# count the subjects of each combination of test results
d <- baysesp_data(
  data = study,
  tests = c("A", "B"),
  verified = "verified",
  disease = "disease"
)

# saturated model, verification that depends only on the test results
fit <- baysesp(data = d, model = saturated(verification = mar()), seed = 1)

test_accuracy(fit = fit)                                  # Se, Sp, PPV, NPV
rule_accuracy(fit = fit, rules = list(any_positive(), all_positive()))
compare_tests(fit = fit, first = "A", second = "B")
plot(fit)

The package website has the documentation of every function and a vignette that goes through all the features of the package, vignette("baysesp").

The package is under active development and its interface may still change.
